title: Stock Market Today, Sept. 24: BlackBerry Lifts Fiscal 2027 Guidance on Record QNX Revenue
author: Josh Kohn-Lindquist
description: BlackBerry (BB) surged 4.18% after beating Q2 earnings expectations with 26% revenue growth and 81% adjusted EBITDA growth, while lifting full-year fiscal 2027 guidance. The company's QNX unit achieved 27% sales growth and is expanding beyond automotive into autonomous vehicles, robotics, and AI applications. However, the analyst notes caution at the current 46x forward earnings valuation.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q2 earnings beat with 26% revenue and 81% EBITDA growth, raised full-year guidance, record QNX revenue with 27% growth, and expansion into high-growth markets like autonomous vehicles and robotics. However, valuation at 46x forward earnings is noted as a concern.
Closed down 0.86% as a sector rival in cybersecurity and embedded software. Mentioned as a comparable company but no specific news or performance drivers discussed.

title: Mplify Announces Winners of the 2026 NaaS Excellence Awards
author: Not Specified

title: CrowdStrike vs. Figma: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Jake Lerch
description: The article compares two high-growth tech stocks: CrowdStrike, a cloud-native cybersecurity leader with $4.8B revenue and strong free cash flow but trading at a 50.3x P/S ratio, versus Figma, a collaborative design platform with 41% revenue growth but significant losses and a 10.5x P/S ratio. CrowdStrike is recommended for growth-oriented investors due to solid fundamentals, while Figma faces risks from frontier AI models disrupting its core design workflow.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong revenue growth (21.7%), substantial free cash flow ($1.3B), low debt-to-equity ratio (0.2x), market leadership as second-largest cybersecurity stock, and positioning in AI security infrastructure. Despite July 2024 incident and premium valuation, fundamentals support growth investor appeal.

title: This Dividend King Was Removed From the S&P 100. Here's Why It's a Great Buy for Long-Term Investors Anyway.
author: Leo Sun
description: Colgate-Palmolive was removed from the S&P 100 index due to its $69 billion market cap being eclipsed by faster-growing AI-driven stocks, but the company remains a solid long-term investment. With 63 consecutive years of dividend increases, a 347% total return over 20 years, and expected 17% EPS CAGR through 2028, the stock offers stability and growth potential despite being a slower-growth consumer staples company.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite S&P 100 removal, the company demonstrates strong fundamentals with 63 years of consecutive dividend increases, healthy earnings growth projections (17% CAGR through 2028), stable recession-resistant business model, and reasonable valuation at 22x forward earnings. Removal was due to relative underperformance versus AI stocks, not business deterioration.

title: Where Will SentinelOne (S) Stock Be in 3 Years?
author: Leo Sun
description: SentinelOne, an AI-powered cybersecurity company, has seen its stock decline from a 2021 high of $76.30 to around $24, trading below its $35 IPO price. While revenue grew from $93M to $1B over five years, growth has decelerated to an expected 20-21% for fiscal 2027, signaling the end of hypergrowth days. The company faces intense competition from larger players like Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike, macro headwinds affecting enterprise spending, and declining net revenue retention among enterprise customers. Analysts project modest 18% revenue CAGR through 2029, with the stock potentially reaching $15.4B market cap (86% gain) within three years if current trends hold, but remaining well below its all-time high.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock trades significantly below IPO price and all-time high; hypergrowth phase has ended with decelerating revenue growth (20-21% expected); facing intense competition from larger cybersecurity firms; declining net revenue retention among enterprise customers (115% to 109%); not expected to achieve profitability within three years; valuation at 6.9x sales is not compelling.
